species.real: Stingrays have electric sensors on their undersides that pick up the faint electrical fields of animals buried in the sand.
species.name: Raylette

dex.text: Flaps up to strangers in the shallows expecting a snack. Has learned that humans arrive with tuna and leave with a story.
dex.fact: At Stingray City, a sandbar in the North Sound of Grand Cayman, southern stingrays gather where fishers once cleaned their catch, and now come for visitors' squid.

species.real: Female southern stingrays grow much bigger than males, with a span that can reach about one and a half metres.
species.name: Sandbarray

dex.text: Glides like a wet duvet and charges for hugs in squid. Quite harmless unless you step on its sandbar, which is entirely its sandbar.
dex.fact: Southern stingrays have a barbed spine on the tail, but at Stingray City they are used to people and are usually calm; the safe move is to shuffle your feet in the sand.
